Alright, let me think through this year like I do every year. I'll talk it out first, then write it down proper.

---

My name don't matter much, but I've been working these 7 mu outside the village my whole life — well, since I was twenty. 35 years. My father worked this same land before me. It's wheat after maize after wheat, year after year. That's just how it goes here in Quzhou.

I only finished primary school, so I don't bother with all them kg-per-mu calculations the agriculture station people talk about on the loudspeaker. I go by what I see in my field and what my neighbors do. My cousin Lao Wang, he farms maybe 12 mu just up the road, and we talk almost every day at the shop. If something new works for him, I might try it small first. If it don't work for him, I don't touch it.

**Wheat first — that's the backbone.**

I plant wheat around the 8th or 10th of October, right after the maize comes off. I always have. My neighbors plant around the same time. If you plant too early, it grows too tall before winter and freezes back. Too late, the roots don't set good. Mid-October, that's the right window.

Seed — I buy from the agri-supply shop in town. They carry 良星99 and a couple others. I usually get whatever bag the shopkeeper says people are buying this year, maybe 10 kg per mu. I don't save seed anymore, the yields are better with the new bags. Maybe 50 yuan per mu for seed.

Fertilizer — here's how I do it: one bag of compound (the 15-15-15) per mu before planting. That's 50 kg per mu, though honestly I spread it by eye, two bags for every three mu, something like that. Then at jointing in March when the wheat is coming back and getting tall, I spread half a bag of urea per mu as topdress. Maybe 20 kg. If the wheat looks yellow I might add a little more, if it looks dark green I skip it. That's two applications. My neighbor Lao Li, he does three applications now because his son told him to — I tried that one year and didn't see the difference in my field, so I went back to two.

Irrigation — wheat needs water, no way around it. The well is metered and it costs money. I always water right after planting to get it going, then once in spring when it's greening up, and then once at grain filling in May. Three times. If it rains good in spring I might skip one, but you can't count on that. Each watering is maybe 50 yuan of pump time per mu.

Pesticide — spring weeds in wheat are bad, so I spray herbicide once when it warms up in March. If I see rust or aphids late in the season I spray once more, but most years one spray is enough. I don't go overboard on sprays, they cost money.

Tillage — I hire the tractor guy to come rotary till before I plant. 50 yuan a mu. I don't own a tractor, nobody with 7 mu owns a tractor.

Harvest — I hire the combine. 60 yuan a mu. My son comes back from his job in town for the day.

Yield — last year I got maybe 430 kg per mu, year before was better, about 470. I'm expecting around 430, maybe 450 if the spring rain is good. My neighbors with better land get 500, but my field is on the lower side.

**Now maize — summer crop, tight turnaround.**

The minute wheat is off in early June, maize has to go in within a week. No time to plow proper. I use the planter behind a neighbor's small tractor — the planter drops seed and fertilizer together right into the wheat stubble. No tillage. Pay him 40 yuan a mu for the planting.

Seed — hybrid, 郑单958 or whatever the shop has that's similar. About 3 kg per mu, maybe 50 yuan per mu.

Fertilizer — I put down about 40 kg of compound (15-15-15) per mu at planting along with the seed. Then when the maize is about knee-high, around mid-July, I go through with the urea cart and spread maybe 20 kg per mu next to the rows. Two applications. Some of the business farms around here do one-shot slow-release fertilizer but it costs more and I don't trust it.

Irrigation — if it rains in July and August I don't water maize at all. But if July is dry, I water once at tasseling, that's the critical time. Some years two. I'll plan for one and see.

Pesticide — one herbicide spray after planting to keep the weeds down. If I see corn borer in July I'll spray insecticide, but not always. 

Harvest — hire the combine again, end of September. Sometimes my wife and I hand-pick the edges where the machine misses.

Yield — 450 to 500 kg per mu most years. Maize does well on this land if the weather is normal.

**Money and labor.**

We have 3 people in the household — me, my wife, and my younger son who works in town most of the year. My wife helps during harvest and spraying. Son comes back for the busy weeks. I do most of the day-to-day myself. 7 mu isn't much, one man can handle it except for the crunch times.

I try to spend no more than 7000 yuan a year on inputs across both crops. Any more and I'm eating into the reserve. The compound fertilizer and the urea, that's the biggest bill. Then irrigation. Then seed and hired machinery.

I don't take big risks. If something worked last year, I do it again. If it didn't, I change one thing, not five things. That's how my father farmed and it's how I farm.
